original_test_intent: Validate every SMBIOS Type 44 Processor Additional Information record references the correct Type 4 processor and carries the approved processor-specific block, with stable topology/content after reboot.
original_method: Preserve logs, collect complete raw Type 44 and referenced Type 4 structures on the verified SUT, resolve every handle to an exact socket/processor, parse block length/architecture/contents against the recipe, reboot once with approval and repeat.
manual_activity: The owner supplies processor topology and Type 44 block semantics and approves reboot/recovery; automation then performs handle-aware read-only comparison.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, socket/processor population, BIOS/SMBIOS and dmidecode identities
Expected Type 44 record count, referenced handles and processor-specific block bytes/decoded fields
Block length, architecture identifier, optional/unknown and ordering rules
Approved reboot, workload window, boot deadline and independent recovery
safety_requirements: Preserve dmesg, syslog and SEL; no log clearing
Keep collection read-only; never change CPU/firmware/SMBIOS configuration
Use protected credentials and evidence handling for processor identifiers
Fail closed on orphan/duplicate handles, malformed block lengths, unsupported architecture or parser truncation
Require reboot approval and stop on topology drift, wrong target or recovery failure
No automatic retry or guessed block decoding
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, topology, owner block schema and reboot approval
Collect complete raw Type 44 and referenced Type 4 records
Resolve handle-to-socket identity and parse every block with raw preservation
Make no firmware mutation, retry or PASS/FAIL verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Type 4 topology and Type 44 architecture/block schema
Review handle/block/topology/persistence deviations and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `dmidecode -t 44` is relevant, but `grep -A1` omits complete handles and block payload, does not collect referenced Type 4 or compare reboot persistence, and uses insecure SSH.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely archive complete raw Type 44 and Type 4 structures before/after the approved reboot, resolve every handle, validate block boundaries and decode only through the approved architecture schema.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Referenced Handle, Processor-Specific Block, reboot persistence, source script and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Normalize Type 44 records by referenced Type 4 socket identity, retain raw block bytes and validated length, decode owner-approved architecture fields and compare the complete per-socket set across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds cross-structure handle resolution and raw block integrity while rejecting filtered evidence and log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A Type 44 heading cannot reveal an orphan handle, swapped socket association, truncated block, wrong architecture decode or hidden additional record.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Processor-Specific Block layout is architecture-specific; generic parsing or byte interpretation without the approved schema can produce false conclusions.

project_override_considerations: Optional records, socket-order changes or block-version transitions must be tied to exact processor/BIOS recipe and remain visible in the normalized diff; handle integrity cannot be waived.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/socket/processor/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode identity plus approved Type 4/44 matrix
Complete pre-reboot Type 44 raw blocks and resolved Type 4 handle/socket mapping
Approved reboot/boot timeline and same-target proof
Preserved logs, no-write/no-clear/no-auto-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently require Type 44 handle/block correctness and reboot persistence. The prior command is incomplete but not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Processor topology, block schema and reboot approval are normal package/user inputs that gate execution but not static review.

review_improvement: Preserves both named Type 44 elements and adds exact Type 4 handle/socket resolution, block-boundary validation and architecture-controlled decoding.
independent_technical_reasoning: The same processor-specific block bytes can be incorrectly assigned if a Referenced Handle points to another Type 4 record, so content-only equality is insufficient. Multi-socket systems also need a stable semantic socket identity rather than relying on output order. Raw block length and bytes must be retained because architecture-specific decoding can change with parser versions while the firmware table stays constant.
